# hands/rent

people Teeny rents on RentAHuman.ai.

## Not available to you

The exec fence refuses `hands/rent` to you: a call is blocked before it runs. Its jobs and the operator run it. Do not try it, and do not look for another way to do what it would do. What follows is for reference only.

## How it is called (reference)

The operator and the jobs invoke it from the repository root as `hands/rent <verb> [flags]`.

- A verb that takes a body reads one JSON object from stdin. Everything else is flags.
- It prints one JSON object on stdout. Exit 0 is success. Exit 2 is a refusal by a rule, the guard or a cap: read the `rule` and `reason`, and do not retry it unchanged. Any other exit is an error.
- Secrets belong to the hand; you never see them and never pass one.
- The hand runs the guard, its caps and `DRY_RUN` itself. `DRY_RUN` is on unless the box turned it off; under it an acting verb checks every rule and sends nothing. Do not try to go around the hand, and do not look for another way to do what it refused.

## Side effects

- Acting (side effects in the world, each goes through the guard and the caps): post; accept; review; message
- Job (writes state or calls the core): poll
- Operator only (never call): resolve ID --as paid|submitted; cancel ID [--reason R]
- Read only: status; list [--status S], get ID; humans [--skill --city --country --limit N]

## Verbs

| Verb | Kind | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `post` | A | `{title, brief, done, price_usd, city, state, country}` (or `remote: true`; optional `proof` [photo, video, text, link], `proof_details`, `hours`, `category`, `skills`). |
| `accept` | A | `{job, application}`: hires one applicant from the money already held (`accept_application`, its own key). |
| `review` | A | `{job, verdict: approve\|redo\|reject, reason, submission}`: against the bounty's done-criteria. |
| `message` | A | `{job, text}`: to the person hired, through the guard, with a key so a retry sends once. |
| `poll` | J | Every open job, once: a post whose answer was lost is sent again with its own key (RentAHuman answers with the first bounty); applications, submitted work and the worker's messages become `rent` stimuli, each stranger's word through `guard inbound` first (a held one is never sho… |
| `status` | R | The caps, today's spend, open jobs, jobs in doubt, and the RentAHuman wallet (`get_wallet`). |
| `list [--status S]`, `get ID` | R | The jobs, newest first; one with what `poll` has passed on. |
| `humans [--skill --city --country --limit N]` | R | Who is on RentAHuman (`list_humans`). |
| `resolve ID --as paid\|submitted` | O | Settles a job `in_doubt` (or stuck `paying`) after the operator checked it on rentahuman.ai. |
| `cancel ID [--reason R]` | O | Ends an unhired bounty (`cancel_bounty`, confirmed with its token). |

Kinds: R = read: no side effect beyond its read cache; A = acting: posts, sends, pays or opens something in the world; O = operator-only: the operator runs it, never you; J = job: writes state or calls the core, says nothing to anyone; scheduled jobs run it, you do not.

Verbs named in the hand's source: `accept`, `cancel`, `get`, `humans`, `list`, `message`, `poll`, `post`, `resolve`, `review`, `status`.

Flags named in the hand's source: `--as`, `--city`, `--country`, `--limit`, `--reason`, `--skill`, `--status`.

For one verb's exact flags, run `hands/rent <verb> --help` (never put a VAR= in front of a command: the shell refuses it, and DRY_RUN is not yours to set). The full account is in docs/hands.md.
